# Parent-checked primary-source notes
These are scope summaries, not new theorem claims; URLs and exact locators permit later source checking.

Dummit, Dummit, Kisilevsky, Signature ranks of units in cyclotomic extensions of abelian number fields, Pacific J Math298(2019), pp285-298. https://msp.org/pjm/2019/298-2/pjm-v298-n2-p03-s.pdf . Actual Proposition3, journal291/PDFpage8: for m=2^a, a>=2, circular units in Q(zeta_m)^+ have maximal signature rank 2^(a-2). Following paragraph gives Hasse norm-minus-one circular unit (zeta_(2m)^5-zeta_(2m)^-5)/(zeta_(2m)-zeta_(2m)^-1), and its Galois conjugate signatures span. Over F2 only simple representation of a2group is trivial. This is NOT Weber class-number-one conjecture. A polynomial construction of the explicit units plus full signatures can pay real unit squareclasses; CM transfer and torsion must still be proved.

Sharifi, Iwasawa notes Chapter4 https://math.ucla.edu/~sharifi/notes/iwasawa-ch04.html . Actual Theorem4.3.3 states circular-real-unit index equals real class number for FULL odd-prime-power cyclotomic fields. Its displayed scope is odd p, not p2 and not arbitrary subfields. Do not transfer this to arbitrary binary prime conductor subfields without source/proof, nor treat a length-p cyclotomic product as polynomial in logp.

Simon, Rational points on conics and generalizations, workshop2005 notes by Stamminger edited Stoll, https://www.mathe2.uni-bayreuth.de/stoll/workshop2005/ConicsSimon.pdf . Actual Section2: relative conic X²-aY²=bZ² is a relative norm equation; an S-unit target need not be norm of an S-unit without a condition on the extension's S-class2part. The short note does NOT prove a general polynomial BIT relative-conic algorithm. Rational Cremona-Rusin algorithm is separately fully checked in the supplied conic proof.

Biasse-Fieker-Hofmann-Page, Norm relations and computational problems in number fields, arxiv2002.12332v4. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.12332 . Actual Theorem4.18 is GRH-conditional polynomial reduction given a suitable norm relation and subfield S-unit input. It is not a free subfield-unit algorithm. The actual subgroup criterion excludes cyclic groups: a faithful one-dimensional character kills every norm element of a nontrivial subgroup, hence precludes any rational identity with those norm elements. For noncyclic2groups, even denominators cannot simply be inverted modulo2. No full decomposition algorithm is supplied by this summary.

# Quadratic squareclasses by rational norm conics

2026-11-13. Independent mathematical attack on the parent's proposed
quadratic bypass. The exact sequence and a stronger primitive-numerator
lifting lemma survive. The algebra below is proved directly. A polynomial
algorithm is **conditional here** on a source-verified rational-conic search
backend with the stated bit clock. The parent is separately checking that
source. No API report, ACCEPT label, or finite example proves that clock.

Read context: `research/STATE.md` (current top state), `research/TRAPS.md`,
`research/GOAL.md`, and `research/GENERAL_NATIVE_SELMER_COMPOSITION.md`.
No archives, Git, network, or external API were used for this review.

## 1. Exact scope and statement

Let d be a nonzero squarefree integer other than 1, K=Q(sqrt(d)), and use
the maximal order for prime-ideal valuations. Let S_Q be a finite set of
rational primes containing every prime dividing 2 disc(K), equivalently
every prime dividing 2d. Let S contain ALL prime ideals over S_Q. Define

    U = Q(S_Q,2) = {q in Q*: v_p(q) even for p outside S_Q}/Q*^2,
    W = K(S,2) = {alpha in K*: v_P(alpha) even for P outside S}/K*^2.

Let V be the subgroup of U consisting of squareclasses having a rational
representative in N(K*). This is independent of the representative:
every rational square t^2 is N(t). Then there is an exact sequence

    0 -> U/<[d]> --inclusion--> W --norm--> V -> 0.

Thus, for s=|S_Q|,

    dim_F2 W = s + dim_F2 V.

The support condition is essential. No real-place sign restriction is
imposed on W itself; signs enter only in V through norm solvability.

## 2. Descent of the norm and injection on the rational kernel

For alpha in W and p outside S_Q,

    v_p(N alpha) = sum_(P|p) f_P v_P(alpha)

is even. Hence norm indeed maps W into U and its image lies in V.

A rational q in U belongs to W because v_P(q)=e_P v_p(q), so outside S
all valuations are even. If q is a square in K, write q=(x+y sqrt(d))^2
with x,y rational. Its sqrt(d) coefficient gives 2xy=0. Therefore q is
either a rational square or d times a rational square. Conversely d is a
square in K, and [d] belongs to U by the support hypothesis. This proves
the claimed injection U/<[d]> -> W, including d<0 and K=Q(i).

## 3. Complete norm kernel, with an elementary proof

Suppose alpha in W has square norm, N(alpha)=c^2 with c in Q*.
If alpha=-c, it is already rational. Otherwise put

    q = Tr(alpha) + 2c.

Then

    (alpha+c)^2 = q alpha.

Since alpha+c is nonzero in a field, q is nonzero. Thus [alpha]=[q] in
K*/K*^2. This is a direct version of the Hilbert-90 argument, requiring
no constructive Hilbert-90 oracle.

For P outside S over p, all such primes are unramified, so e_P=1.
Taking valuations in the displayed square relation gives

    v_p(q) + v_P(alpha) = 2 v_P(alpha+c).

Since v_P(alpha) is even, v_p(q) is even. Hence [q] is in U. The special
case alpha=-c has the same parity conclusion directly. The kernel is
therefore exactly the rational image; there is no extra real-field,
torsion, ordinary-class-group, or negative-Pell term missing from it.

## 4. Stronger lift: no denominator factoring is needed

Take [a] in V and choose its signed squarefree integer representative a,
whose prime support is contained in S_Q. By definition there is a
rational solution of x^2-d y^2=a. Clearing denominators and removing the
common gcd gives a primitive integer point

    X^2 - d Y^2 = a Z^2,       gcd(X,Y,Z)=1.

Here Z is nonzero: otherwise nonsquare d forces X=Y=0. Define simply

    beta = X + Y sqrt(d).

This algebraic integer is already in W, and N(beta)=a Z^2 gives its
required norm squareclass. In particular, **do not factor Z or multiply
by a product of denominator primes**: those operations are unnecessary.

Proof: let p be outside S_Q. Then p is odd and does not divide ad. If
p divided both X and Y, the conic equation would imply p|Z, contrary to
primitivity. If p is inert, divisibility of beta by the unique prime
over p would mean X=Y=0 in the two-dimensional residue field over F_p,
again impossible. So its valuation is zero at inert p.

If p splits as P Pbar, both primes cannot divide beta: that would imply
beta is zero modulo p and hence p|X,Y. Therefore one of v_P(beta) and
v_Pbar(beta) is zero. The other is even, since

    v_P(beta)+v_Pbar(beta)=v_p(N beta)=2 v_p(Z).

This proves the required parity at every prime outside S. Ramified and
dyadic primes are all in S and impose no condition in this argument.

The original proposed normalization of alpha=beta/Z also works: at
each outside split denominator prime its valuations are (-k,+k), and
multiplication by p for odd k clears the parities. The numerator proof
is stronger because it avoids identifying or factoring those primes.

## 5. Exact linear algebra and constructive output

Use the basis -1 and the primes in S_Q for U. The standard quadratic
local-global theorem says

    [a] in V  iff  (a,d)_v = +1 for every place v of Q.

Equivalently this is Hasse--Minkowski for the ternary form
X^2-dY^2-aZ^2; a nonzero isotropic vector automatically has Z nonzero.
It is enough to test v in S_Q together with infinity: outside S_Q both
a and d are units at an odd prime, so the Hilbert symbol is +1.

Bilinearity makes these conditions a binary matrix with s+1 columns
and at most s+1 rows. Odd-prime Hilbert symbols use valuations and
Legendre symbols; the dyadic row uses the usual odd-unit residues mod8;
the real row is nonzero only when both arguments are negative. There is
no global class group or fundamental unit in this matrix computation.

Choose a complement to [d] in U by binary elimination and use its
rational representatives as the first s basis elements of W. Compute a
basis [a_1],...,[a_r] of V. For each a_j, get a primitive conic point and
output beta_j=X_j+Y_j sqrt(d) as above. Together these give a COMPLETE
basis of W. Independence follows by applying norm, then the injection
of U/<[d]>. Spanning follows by cancelling the norm of an arbitrary
class with a product of the beta_j, leaving the complete rational
kernel from section 3. No field-square independence test is needed.

The local-global theorem is used as a standard mathematical theorem
here. The parent owns its primary-source attribution and, separately,
the effective search theorem; this review did not browse for sources.

## 6. Bit resources and the precise conditional algorithm

Let L include log|d|, the summed bit lengths of the primes in S_Q, and
any conversion from the native quadratic polynomial to sqrt(d).
Assume that integer factorization is paid, and that a proved backend
finds a nonzero rational point on each solvable input conic in time
polynomial in its coefficient bit length, with controlled error and
only polynomially many factoring calls on polynomial-bit integers.
Alternatively, one may use its stronger actually verified interface if
it needs only factorizations of the original coefficients. Do not infer
that stronger interface from this proof.

There are at most s+1 conic calls; every a_j is a product of selected
input primes and a sign, so log|a_j|<=L. The matrix and all local tests
have polynomial bit cost. A polynomial-time backend necessarily returns
polynomial-bit coordinates. Clearing the three denominators and taking
their common gcd preserves polynomial bit size. Each beta_j therefore
has polynomial-bit explicit coordinates. There is no Pell-sized output,
unit expansion, ideal principality search, or support-factorization bill
for these beta_j. Exact conic residuals can be checked before using them.

For a native monic quadratic t^2+b t+c, write its discriminant as m^2 d
using paid integer factoring. In its native field,

    sqrt(d) = (2 theta+b)/m.

The conversion has polynomial bit size. This proof constructs global
squareclasses without computing the maximal order, although the global
Selmer pipeline may still need it for its separately paid local frames.

Consequently the global quadratic-squareclass stage is a classical
polynomial reduction to factoring plus the precisely specified conic
backend. If a primary-source theorem verifies that conic backend as a
polynomial factoring-oracle algorithm, it gives the corresponding
unconditional factoring-oracle upper bound. Replacing factoring by Shor
then gives a quantum polynomial stage without quantum S-unit or
class-group algorithms and without GRH. The parent must first verify
the source's actual bit clock, factoring requirements, output model,
randomness/error guarantee, and both signs of d. These are not supplied
by a conic software command or this finite control.

## 7. Real-field attack and the one durable exact control

Let d=34 and S_Q={2,17}. The equation X^2-34Y^2=-Z^2 has primitive point
(3,1,5). Hence beta=3+sqrt(34) has norm -25, and

    (beta) = (5, sqrt(34)+3)^2.

Thus beta belongs to W, including at the outside prime5. Meanwhile the
continued-fraction period of sqrt(34) is (1,4,1,10), of even length, so
the INTEGRAL negative-Pell equation x^2-34y^2=-1 has no solution.
Integral norm-minus-one units are therefore not a prerequisite for the
required virtual squareclass. Rational beta/5 has norm exactly -1.

Also N(6+sqrt(34))=2 and N(sqrt(34))=-34. These norm squareclasses span
U=<-1,2,17>, so dim V=3 and the theorem gives dim W=2+3=5. This dimension
is a deduction from the exact sequence, not a computed class-group
oracle result. No class group was needed for this control.

Durable one-example script and exact output:

- `2026-11-13-quadratic-norm-squareclasses-control.sage`
- `2026-11-13-quadratic-norm-squareclasses-control.json`

Command, from the repository root:

    /opt/anaconda3/envs/qsearch-cas/bin/sage research/audits/reviews/2026-11-13-quadratic-norm-squareclasses-control.sage > research/audits/reviews/2026-11-13-quadratic-norm-squareclasses-control.json

All final assertions passed. The control falsifies an integral-negative-
Pell prerequisite; it is not evidence for the universal bit clock.

## 8. Boundaries and next decisive work

The full-ramified-support assumption cannot be removed silently. For
K=Q(sqrt(35)) with S_Q={2}, the rational class5 is admissible in K(S,2)
because its valuation at the ramified prime over5 is2, but it has no
representative in Q({2},2) modulo the field-square relation35. The
displayed rational-kernel statement would fail. Likewise, S must contain
both primes over every selected split prime for the claimed rational
inclusion to be valid as written.

No extension to cubic/general branch fields follows. No local-image
algorithm, full Selmer composition, classical lower bound, practical
implementation, novelty, speedup, or negative-Pell decision algorithm
is claimed. The output retains the SAME complete native K(S,2) space;
it is not a weakened unit-only problem.

Next hard question: verify an original conic-search source at the
polynomial-bit factoring-oracle interface. Acceptance test: an actual
algorithm/theorem supplying a valid nonzero point for every locally
solvable diagonal ternary form, with controlled coordinate lengths and
the stated total bit/factorization cost. Mechanical follow-up after the
parent's source disposition: retain the one exact control, link the
proof/source in the composition note, and preserve all false gates.
The parent will record this checkpoint in the shared handoff, mechanical
queue, and state to avoid concurrent edits by this helper.

# One-prime two-class coverage and a ramified-support counterexample

2026-11-13. Independent focused review of the two new algebraic claims in
`audits/openai_runs/2026-11-13-general-two-coverage/response.md`, read in
full. STATE/TRAPS and the current global composition were consulted. No
Git, network, external API, archives, numerical sweep, or shared-note edit.

**Decision:** both claims are correct at their stated scope. The first
removes the class-generator GRH requirement for the specified Galois
2-power branch fields. The second genuinely defeats using only the native
bad-prime support as a general two-primary source. Neither supplies a
general unconditional source or a quantum-advantage result.

## 1. The special-base-Q odd-class-number proof

Let K/Q be finite Galois, with degree a power of 2, and with at most one
finite ramified rational prime p. Let C be its ORDINARY ideal class group.
For proof only, take the maximal ordinary unramified elementary 2-extension
M/K, corresponding under class field theory to C/2C. This extension is
canonical under automorphisms of K; hence M/Q is Galois, with a finite
2-group Gamma. Write H=Gal(M/K). No Hilbert class field is constructed by
the algorithm.

M/Q is unramified away from p at finite primes. Let I be inertia at one
prime of M above p. If I were proper, choose a maximal subgroup N of Gamma
containing I. In a finite 2-group, every maximal subgroup is normal of
index 2. It therefore contains every conjugate of I. The quadratic field
M^N/Q would be unramified at p and at every other finite prime.

That is impossible: every nontrivial quadratic number field has a
fundamental discriminant of absolute value greater than 1. Thus I=Gamma.
Since M/K is unramified, its relative inertia group is `I intersect H=1`.
It follows that H=1, so `C/2C=0` and C has odd order. If no finite prime
ramifies, the same quadratic-quotient argument first gives K=Q.

This also proves that the sole possible ramified finite prime is totally
ramified, with just one prime above it, whenever the extension is
nontrivial. Thus no separate nonsplitting hypothesis is missing in this
special base-Q argument. It would be incorrect to delete that hypothesis
from a more general Iwasawa statement over arbitrary base fields: the
argument here specifically uses the absence of finite-unramified quadratic
extensions of Q. The class-number result is known mathematics, not a
novelty claim. This proof does not rely on the report's cyclic-cubic-163
example, which is not re-audited here.

## 2. Exactly what this pays in the native Selmer composition

Let S contain the primes of K above the native rational set
`P0={p:p divides 2 disc(f)}`. It may contain many primes in addition to the
single prime ramified in K/Q: cross-resultants between distinct branch
factors can enlarge P0. This causes no difficulty. Since C is odd, its
quotient by the classes of S is odd as well.

The natural map is an isomorphism

    O_(K,S)^*/O_(K,S)^{*2}  ~=  K(S,2).

Injection is immediate: a field square root of an S-unit is an S-unit.
For surjection, if alpha has even valuations outside S, let a be the ideal
with half those outside-S valuations. Then `2[a]` lies in the subgroup
J generated by S. The quotient C/J is odd, so `[a]` itself lies in J.
Choose an S-supported b in its class and `(beta)=a b^-1`; then
`alpha/beta^2` is an S-unit. The witnesses a,b,beta are used only to prove
completeness. They are not uncharged computed generators.

Consequently the source is literally `T=S`, with no extra-prime parity
rows for this factor and no randomized class-generator coverage step.
This does NOT claim that the full class group is trivial or generated by
S. It also does NOT compute a complete S-unit basis for free.

The remaining operation is exactly the already reviewed complete compact
S-unit computation, including the torsion squareclass bit. The retained
actual Biasse--Song Theorem 1 has polynomial dependence on degree,
log discriminant, |S| and the largest logarithmic prime norm, without a
GRH premise. Its separate class-group-generation application is where
GRH entered; see the retained `global-primary.md` source packet, physical
lines 28--31 and 191--196. The native maximal-order, compact evaluation,
norm/sign, real-image and all-prime local-image interfaces remain the same
ones checked in the general composition.

These costs stay native: factor the original polynomial and discriminant,
compute its orders and prime decompositions, and take all primes over P0.
There are at most `deg(K)*|P0|` of them, and
`log Norm(P)<=deg(K)*log p`. Both are polynomial in native input length;
there is no enumeration up to the numerical value of a large p. The
complete unit call pays arbitrary additional S-primes, not just the one
ramified prime.

Therefore, on every native odd-degree monic squarefree input whose branch
fields are all of the following types, the reviewed global quantum
Selmer-dimension composition is unconditional:

* Q, handled directly;
* Galois 2-power extensions of Q with at most one finite ramified prime,
  handled with T=S;
* the cubic fields covered by the separately retained unconditional cubic
  source, using THAT source to choose T, which need not equal S.

The field properties restrict the correctness domain; no class groups,
units, normal closures or field automorphisms are supplied as advice. The
explicit family below has directly recognizable membership. This review
does not add a general family-recognition algorithm or re-prove the cubic
source. The output is the exact Selmer dimension with bounded error
polynomial in native input bits and log(1/eta). Global compact-unit
completeness remains probabilistic, so this is not promoted to an
abort-only global guarantee. No GRH class-generator step remains on this
domain; no general unconditional source is inferred outside it.

## 3. The quadratic native counterexample

Take distinct primes `p,q congruent 1 (mod 8)` with `(p/q)=1`. Quadratic
reciprocity gives `(q/p)=1`. Set

    K=Q(sqrt(pq)),       M=Q(sqrt(p),sqrt(q)).

The three quadratic discriminants are p, q and pq, so the biquadratic
discriminant formula gives

    Delta_K=pq,         Delta_M=p*q*pq=(pq)^2.

The tower discriminant identity therefore gives relative discriminant 1:
M/K is unramified at every finite prime. Both fields are totally real,
and every real place splits, so this is an ORDINARY unramified quadratic
extension, not merely a narrow-class construction. It is nontrivial
because distinct p and q give a degree-four biquadratic field.

The local Frobenius claims hold exactly:

* At p, q is a square in Q_p by its nonzero quadratic residue and Hensel's
  lemma. Thus `K_P=Q_p(sqrt(p))`, and adjoining sqrt(p) already splits the
  relative quadratic algebra. The unique prime above p splits in M/K.
* At q the same argument, with p and q interchanged, applies.
* At 2, both p and q are squares in Q_2 because they are 1 modulo 8.
  Hence `K tensor Q_2=Q_2 times Q_2` and
  `M tensor Q_2=Q_2^4`. Each of the two primes of K over 2 splits in M/K.

Thus the nontrivial Artin character `psi:Cl(K)->{+1,-1}` is trivial on
EVERY prime above 2pq, including every prime ramified in K/Q. Their class
span has even index. In fact `Cl(O_(K,S))` has nonzero 2-torsion, so the
standard exact sequence shows that S-unit squareclasses strictly miss
part of K(S,2). This is a failure of the proposed source, not merely a
failure of one attempted proof of its completeness.

The native polynomial is

    f=x(x^2-pq),        disc(f)=4(pq)^3.

It is monic and squarefree, with branch algebra Q times K and native
bad-prime support exactly {2,p,q}. The corresponding elliptic equation
has discriminant `16 disc(f)=64(pq)^3`, so no other finite prime is bad.
For the explicit witness p=17,q=89, reciprocity and `89=4 (mod 17)` give
`(17/89)=(4/17)=1`; both primes are 1 modulo 8. No class-number, Pell,
exceptional-zero or numerical computation is needed for this witness.

For completeness, an odd rational prime ell not dividing pq, with p and q
nonsquare modulo ell splits in K but has nontrivial relative Frobenius in
M/K; mixed signs give an inert K-prime whose relative Frobenius is trivial.
This matches the report's double-nonresidue description. It supplies no
claim that a harmful exceptional zero actually exists.

The counterexample does not by itself prove that a final Selmer dimension
computed from an incomplete source is wrong: subsequent norm/local
conditions could remove omitted classes. It refutes the general source
identity and odd-index coverage needed for the stated completeness proof.
It is not hardness or an impossibility theorem for other classical sources.

## 4. Cyclotomic specialization and the classical boundary

For `f_k=x(x^(2^k)+1)`, k>=1, the nontrivial branch factor is
`Phi_(2^(k+1))`, so its field is `Q(zeta_(2^(k+1)))`, of degree 2^k,
Galois and ramified only at 2. Its discriminant has absolute value
`2^(k*2^k)`, and the cross-resultant with x is 1. Thus the literal native
family has P0={2}, and T=S applies. Its complexity is polynomial in the
native degree/coefficients, not in the short exponent k alone.

This family needs a serious classical circular-unit comparison. In the
literal family the only extra S-direction is especially simple:
`Norm(1-zeta)=2`, so `1-zeta` generates the unique prime over 2. A complete
classical mod-square source still needs the relevant circular-unit index
and construction theorem, including its 2-primary index and torsion.
Odd ordinary class number alone is not that unit theorem. For other
polynomial presentations, extra native S-primes must also be paid.
Accordingly this review establishes no advantage for the cyclotomic family
and does not infer free S-unit generators for arbitrary enlarged S.
